title: Getting to Know the SYNC Audio System
introduction:
I use this overview as the cast list for the SYNC-equipped audio system: speakers make the sound, controls accept requests, and separate modules handle audio, display and connected-device functions. The dashboard may look like one stereo, but there is a small ensemble behind it.

Read the component list separately from the feature list, and keep each engine qualifier attached to its entry. This overview identifies equipment and capabilities; it does not supply connector locations, operating thresholds, electrical tests or replacement instructions.

edits.text: The SYNC audio system brings together the components below. I distinguish the audio hardware, display, controls and device connections before looking at the features they support.
edits.why: Separate roles help make sense of a system that appears to the driver as a single dashboard interface.
FCDIM means front control/display interface module. Non-touchscreen describes the display interface; do not assume touch operation.

edits.text: ACM, containing DACMC for 2.3L and 5.2L applications
edits.why: ACM means audio front control module; DACMC means digital audio control module C. Keep the engine qualification attached to the contained module.

edits.text: Radio reception through the AM / FM antenna

edits.why: The Accessory Protocol Interface Module handles connected-device, voice and media functions, including microphone, USB and Bluetooth audio inputs, while working with separate audio and display components.

edits.text: External audio connection: audio input jack

edits.why: The port and its cable are identified together; retain the front connection's identifier when reading a matching service reference.
GPSM means global positioning system module.
This is the separately identified rear connection, including its cable.

edits.text: Audio controls in the RH steering wheel switches
edits.why: RH identifies the right-hand steering wheel controls.

edits.text: Voice input through the SYNC® microphone
edits.why: The microphone supplies input to the connected voice system; the speakers provide its audible output.
This feature's engine restriction is part of the equipment description.
This entry identifies an electrical-load management feature, rather than an audio source.

edits.text: Engine sound enhancement: ESE (2.3L and 5.2L only)
edits.why: Engine sound enhancement and active noise control are separately named features with different applicability.
The feature name identifies speed as the basis for volume compensation; it does not specify adjustment settings.
The APIM explanation above distinguishes connected-device, voice and media functions from the separate audio and display hardware.
